introduction-the-necessary-evil.core: 'You build it, you run it' puts developers on call, which creates ownership and better software, but badly run on-call burns people out. On-call hygiene keeps the load sustainable and fair.

first_principles.problem: Engineers dread their on-call weeks, get paged nightly for noise, and quit.
truths: Sleep loss harms health and judgement.
derivation: **Audit alerts** so only actionable pages wake people.

analogy.title: Being the designated driver
analogy.story: It's a fair duty if shared and acknowledged, and miserable if it's always you and unpaid.
analogy.breaks: Some roles inherently have more on-call, so be transparent at hiring.

check.q: Why does 'you build it, you run it' need on-call hygiene?
check.a: Without sustainable rotations and clean alerts, the ownership model burns engineers out.

rotation-topologies-scheduling-for-sleep.core: Rotation design trades coverage against rest: weekly primary/secondary, follow-the-sun across time zones (no night pages), split day/night shifts, and enough people per rotation (often 6–8+) to keep frequency humane.

first_principles.problem: A 3-person team is on call every third week, with nights included, forever.
truths: Frequency and duration determine the burden.
Night pages are the most harmful.

analogy.title: Hospital night-shift scheduling
analogy.story: Shifts rotate so nobody works every night, with backup doctors on call.
analogy.breaks: Follow-the-sun needs real expertise in every region, not just warm bodies.

example.title: A follow-the-sun rotation
flow: Each region pages only in daytime

check.q: What's the main advantage of follow-the-sun on-call?
check.a: Each region covers its own daytime, largely eliminating night pages.

compensation-models-paying-for-the-pain.core: On-call restricts personal freedom even when quiet (no travel, no drinking, staying near a laptop). Compensate with stipends per shift, pay per page or per hour of response, or time off in lieu, transparently and fairly.

first_principles.problem: Unpaid on-call breeds resentment, especially for those carrying it disproportionately.
truths: Incidents outside hours take personal time.
derivation: **Incident pay or time off** for actual work out of hours.
**Transparency** and alignment with local labour law.

analogy.title: Paying for a standby electrician
analogy.story: You pay them to stay available, and more when they're actually called out.
analogy.breaks: Paying for pages can create a perverse incentive to keep noisy alerts, so pair it with alert quality goals.

example.title: A balanced policy
flow: Hourly pay for out-of-hours incident work
Mandatory late start after 2 AM pages

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Burden is acknowledged and recovery protected.

check.q: Why compensate on-call even if no pages occur?
check.a: Being available restricts personal freedom, which is a cost in itself.

preventing-burnout-the-metrics-of-fatigu.core: Measure on-call health: pages per shift, night or off-hours pages, time spent on incidents, percentage of actionable alerts and repeat alerts, plus surveys. Thresholds (e.g. Google SRE's ≤2 incidents per 12-hour shift) trigger action.

first_principles.problem: Burnout is invisible until someone resigns.
derivation: Set **thresholds** that trigger alert work or staffing.

analogy.title: A fitness tracker for on-call
analogy.story: Sleep, heart rate and recovery metrics warn you before you overtrain.
analogy.breaks: Metrics can be gamed (silencing alerts), so pair them with SLO health.

check.q: Name two metrics that indicate on-call burnout risk.
check.a: For example, pages per shift and the number of off-hours (night) pages, plus a low actionable alert percentage.

the-alert-audit-designing-alerts-that-de.core: Every page is a request to interrupt someone's life, so it must be urgent, actionable, user-impacting and novel. Audit alerts regularly: delete, downgrade to tickets, auto-remediate or improve the noisy ones.

first_principles.problem: Hundreds of alerts fire, most need no action, people learn to ignore them, and real problems get missed.
truths: Not everything needs a human now.
derivation: Ask: does it need **human action now**? Is it **user-impacting**?
**Page** only for urgent symptom alerts (SLO burn).
**Review** every page in weekly on-call handoffs.

analogy.title: A doorbell that rings for every passing car
analogy.story: You'd stop answering it, including when a real visitor arrives.
analogy.breaks: Deleting alerts can remove useful signals, so downgrade before deleting when unsure.

example.title: Auditing the top noisy alerts
flow: Checkout SLO burn → keep as page

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Pages drop 70%, and every remaining one matters.

example.outcome: pages people trust and respond to.

points: Pages must be worth waking for.

check.q: What four qualities should a paging alert have?
check.a: Urgent, actionable, user-impacting and novel (not a repeat of something known).
